label: ACTIVE FRAMEWORK vs LEGACY QTA
rule: Nothing in the active framework may import, open, or take authority from legacy QTA.
note: Which side a file is on is FILE_DISPOSITION.csv's to say, and nothing here restates it per file: the dispositions below name the classes. tools/framework_boundary.py reads both, computes each active production module's static import closure (module-level AND function-level imports, plus the package initialisers every import executes), and fails on any legacy module in it, on any string literal naming a legacy file, and on any import whose module path carries a legacy-ontology token -- the last so that a legacy module moved or renamed out of the disposition's sight is still recognised. Tests are outside the scope: they exercise both sides, and a test of legacy code importing it is the point of the test. TRANSITIONAL modules are measured and reported, not enforced; each is being rewritten or mined for generic physics, and moves to ACTIVE when it no longer reaches legacy.
legacy_ontology_note: The directive's list, as the names they carry in this repository: the machine FSM and its campaign traces (machine_fsm, state_machine_3d), hardware governance and its registries (hardware_governance, hardware_registry, hardware_reviewers), the physical component and apparatus registries (design_component_registry, design.registry, cryo_stack, stage7_boundary, integrated_layers, nv_eligibility), the fixed Mode A/B/C/D orchestration (mode_sequence, future_3d). The BOM, the QTA gate table and the validation registries are legacy FILES and are caught by the file rule, which covers every RETIRE_TO_HISTORY file by name. Mode-letter LABELS inside retained physics (e.g. a mode_d threshold) are not tokens here: they are names, not dependencies, and are removed with the physics they label (directive 27) -- the report counts them.

declared_exceptions.why: It names every tracked file in order to place it on a side of this boundary; it reads none of them, and the legacy names are what it classifies.
An exclusion: the RAG corpus leaves the legacy history bundle OUT. Naming a file to refuse it is the boundary working.

A classifier: its ordered rule table names legacy paths in order to place each file holding the legacy gate-table vocabulary in a class (here the legacy release's checksums, as TOOLING_REFERENCE). It opens every file only to count pattern matches, and the legacy names are what it classifies.

The current-status builder reads the legacy QTA gate table for ONE purpose: to report its historical statuses in the section labelled LEGACY_QTA_ONLY. No current status is computed from it -- tests/test_claim_hygiene.py changes the gate statuses and requires every other section to stay the same -- and nothing in the active framework takes authority from it.

file_rule_note: A legacy file at the repository root is recognised by its file name anywhere (BOM.csv, hardware_registry.json); a nested one only by a path that includes its directory, so a generic SHA256SUMS or release_index.json in some other bundle is not mistaken for the legacy stage-9 release's.
